_source: Staged by the system/browsers/utilities curation pass, 2026-08-15. Merge into registry.json under `apps`, then `make sign-registry` — every entry here has signature:"" and WILL fail `make verify-registry` until signed.
_verification: Every flatpak_id was resolved live against Flathub on 2026-08-15 via GET /api/v2/appstream/<id> (200) and GET /api/v2/summary/<id> (arches, runtime, sandbox permissions), publisher status via GET /api/v2/verification/<id>/status, and extra-data by reading the flathub/<id> build manifest on GitHub. NOT verified: no app was actually installed or launched — that is scripts/verify-app-recipe.sh's job.

flatseal.name: Flatseal
flatseal.description: Flatpak permission editor — review and change what each installed Flatpak app on this box may reach: files, devices, sockets and D-Bus services.
flatseal.author: Martin Abente Lahaye
flatseal._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github/tchx84). Sandbox: filesystems=[xdg-data/flatpak/overrides:create, /var/lib/flatpak/app:ro, xdg-data/flatpak/app:ro]; no network. Edits USER overrides (~/.local/share/flatpak/overrides), which do apply to the system-wide installs FlatpakInstall creates. Talks org.freedesktop.impl.portal.PermissionStore — confirm xdg-desktop-portal actually runs in the streamed session, or the portal pane is inert.

warehouse.name: Warehouse
warehouse.description: Flatpak manager — inspect installed Flatpaks on this box, view and copy their manifests, manage per-app user data, and batch-remove leftovers.
warehouse.author: Heliguy / flattool
warehouse._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github/flattool). Sandbox: filesystems=[~/.var/app, /var/lib/flatpak:ro, ~/.local/share/flatpak:ro, host-etc]; session-bus talk=org.freedesktop.Flatpak (that is full host-side Flatpak control, not a sandboxed subset). COST: runtime is org.gnome.Platform/49 while every other GNOME app here is /50 — installing Warehouse pulls a SECOND ~1.07GB GNOME runtime.

flatsweep.name: Flatsweep
flatsweep.description: Removes leftover data directories that uninstalled Flatpak apps left behind on this box.
flatsweep.author: Giant Pink Robots!
flatsweep._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github/giantpinkrobots). Sandbox: filesystems=[~/.var/app, ~/.local/share/flatpak/app:ro, /var/lib/flatpak/app:ro]; no network. OVERLAP: FlatpakUninstall already runs `flatpak uninstall -y --unused` (flatpak.go:110); Flatsweep covers the ~/.var/app residue that command leaves.

resources.name: Resources
resources.description: System monitor — CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network and per-process usage FOR THIS BOX, not for the machine you are viewing from.
resources.author: nokyan
resources._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (website). Sandbox: filesystems include host:ro — reads the whole box read-only, which is what makes the readings real. STREAMED-MODEL: correct by construction (it reports the box). OVERLAP: duplicates builtin 'system-info' and 'activity'.

chromium.name: Chromium
chromium.description: Open-source web browser — the upstream project Chrome, Brave, Edge and Vivaldi are built from, with no vendor account, sync or telemetry layer.
chromium.author: The Chromium Authors
chromium.license: BSD-3-Clause AND LGPL-2.1+ AND Apache-2.0 AND MIT AND others
chromium._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher NOT verified on Flathub (community-maintained packaging of an open-source project — source is auditable, which is why this is acceptable where an unverified proprietary package would not be). Built from source on Flathub builders; NOT extra-data. Sandbox: filesystems=[home], devices=[all], shared=[ipc,network]. SOVEREIGNTY: this is the entry to recommend over Chrome — same engine, no proprietary blob, no vendor terms.

google-chrome.name: Google Chrome
google-chrome.description: Google's proprietary web browser. The Flathub package is a thin wrapper that downloads Google's binary from dl.google.com at install time; Google's servers and terms govern it, not Vulos.
google-chrome.author: Google LLC
google-chrome._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher NOT verified on Flathub. EXTRA-DATA CONFIRMED by reading the manifest (flathub/com.google.Chrome/master/com.google.Chrome.yaml lines 98 and 112: `type: extra-data`, url dl.google.com, per-arch). So neither Flathub nor Vulos ever holds the payload; the sha256 in the manifest is the only integrity check and it points at Google's server. Sandbox: filesystems include host-etc and xdg-*; devices=[all]; system-bus talk to Avahi/UPower/bluez. Offered for compatibility only — prefer 'chromium'. WITHDRAWN 2026-08-19 UNDER APP-CATALOG POLICY 1a, which this entry was contradicting: the policy excludes proprietary apps for now (founder call 2026-08-15, explicitly reversible) and this app is proprietary AND the only CONFIRMED extra-data app in the catalogue (its manifest fetches the vendor binary from dl.google.com at install time, so nothing about it is redistributable and a mirror would carry an empty shell). It shipped ENABLED in registry.json while APP-CATALOG.md recorded it as removed — the catalogue and the registry disagreeing, with the registry being the one users install from. `_disabled` rather than deleted, so the entry, its measurements and the reversibility survive; with DISABLED-01 the App Hub now shows it as 'Not offered' with a reason instead of an Install button that refuses.

brave.name: Brave
brave.description: Chromium-based browser with ad and tracker blocking on by default. Core browser is MPL-2.0; the optional rewards/VPN features are Brave-operated services.
brave.author: Brave Software
brave._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (website, brave.com). NOT extra-data — the manifest fetches Brave's official release zip per arch at Flathub BUILD time (flathub/com.brave.Browser master, `type: file`, only-arches x86_64/aarch64), so Flathub's own signing does cover the bytes. Sandbox: devices=[all], filesystems include host-etc, /tmp, xdg-desktop; system-bus talk to Avahi/UPower/bluez.

librewolf.name: LibreWolf
librewolf.description: Firefox fork with telemetry, sponsored content and studies removed and stricter privacy defaults compiled in. No vendor account.
librewolf.author: LibreWolf Community
librewolf._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github login provider). NOT extra-data. Sandbox is the TIGHTEST of the six browsers: filesystems=[xdg-download, xdg-run/speech-dispatcher:ro] only — no home, no host. devices=[dri] not [all]. That matters here because a streamed desktop app otherwise runs as root against the box's whole filesystem (see roadmap/APP-CATALOG-SYSTEM-BROWSERS-UTILITIES.md).

vivaldi.name: Vivaldi
vivaldi.description: Proprietary Chromium-based browser with heavy UI customisation, built-in mail, calendar and feed reader. Free of charge, closed source.
vivaldi.author: Vivaldi Technologies
vivaldi._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher NOT verified on Flathub. CORRECTION TO roadmap/APP-CATALOG.md POLICY 1: Vivaldi is NOT extra-data. Its manifest (flathub/com.vivaldi.Vivaldi master, lines 92-109) uses `type: file` on downloads.vivaldi.com .deb per arch, consumed at Flathub BUILD time. Flathub therefore does hold and sign the payload for Vivaldi, unlike Chrome. Verified by reading the manifest, not assumed. Sandbox: devices=[all], filesystems include xdg-desktop and ~/.local/share/applications:create. WITHDRAWN 2026-08-19 UNDER APP-CATALOG POLICY 1a, which this entry was contradicting: the policy excludes proprietary apps for now (founder call 2026-08-15, explicitly reversible) and this app is proprietary (its Flathub build is not extra-data — Flathub holds and signs the payload — but the licence is what policy 1a turns on, not the packaging). It shipped ENABLED in registry.json while APP-CATALOG.md recorded it as removed — the catalogue and the registry disagreeing, with the registry being the one users install from. `_disabled` rather than deleted, so the entry, its measurements and the reversibility survive; with DISABLED-01 the App Hub now shows it as 'Not offered' with a reason instead of an Install button that refuses.

fragments.name: Fragments
fragments.description: Simple BitTorrent client. Torrents download to THIS BOX's disk, not to the machine you are viewing from — use Files to retrieve them.
fragments.author: Felix Häcker
fragments._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (website). Sandbox: filesystems=[host], shared=[network,ipc]. STREAMED-MODEL: description must say downloads land on the box; that is the whole point of a sovereign box, but it is not what a desktop user assumes. OVERLAP: qbittorrent is already in the registry; Fragments is the simple alternative, not a replacement.

bitwarden.name: Bitwarden
bitwarden.description: Password manager client for the Bitwarden service. The app is GPL-3.0, but your vault lives on Bitwarden's servers (or a self-hosted Bitwarden/Vaultwarden) — this is a client, not local-only storage.
bitwarden.author: Bitwarden Inc.
bitwarden._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (website). NOT extra-data — the manifest pulls Bitwarden's GitHub release tarball per arch at BUILD time. Sandbox: devices=[all,dri]; filesystems are NativeMessagingHosts dirs + xdg-download + ~/.mozilla; system-bus talk to login1 and PolicyKit1. SOVEREIGNTY: pairs with the registry's existing self-hostable 'vaultwarden' server entry; keepassxc remains the offline-only option. OVERLAP: builtin 'vault' app.

pika-backup.name: Pika Backup
pika-backup.description: Scheduled deduplicating backups (BorgBackup) of THIS BOX's data to a local disk or a remote host over SSH. It backs up the box, not the device you are viewing from.
pika-backup.author: Small Mammal Collective
pika-backup._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github login provider). Sandbox: filesystems=[host, /var:ro, ~/.var/app, gvfs]; devices=[all]; sockets include ssh-auth; shared=[ipc,network]. STREAMED-MODEL: correct and genuinely useful — a box that backs itself up is the point. NOTE: 'background' is in ValidPermissions but is NOT enforced by anything (manifest.go:19-31 vs the four read sites); scheduled runs depend on the app staying alive in its stream session.

czkawka.name: Czkawka
czkawka.description: Finds duplicate files, empty folders, similar images and broken symlinks on THIS BOX's disks and helps remove them.
czkawka.author: Rafał Mikrut
czkawka._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github login provider). Sandbox: filesystems=[host]; no network. COST: runtime is org.gnome.Platform/49, the same second-runtime problem as Warehouse (~1.07GB on top of /50). DESTRUCTIVE: it deletes files on the box; the Flatpak sandbox grants host, and the streamed session runs as root, so there is no second line of defence.

peazip.name: PeaZip
peazip.description: Archive manager for THIS BOX's filesystem — creates and extracts 7z, zip, tar, rar, iso and ~200 other formats, with AES-256 encrypted archives.
peazip.author: Giorgio Tani
peazip._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github login provider). Sandbox: filesystems=[host, xdg-config/kdeglobals:ro]; no network. RUNTIME: org.kde.Platform/6.10 — shared with the registry's existing qbittorrent entry, so the ~1.05GB is not additional if that is installed. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: org.gnome.FileRoller (GNOME/50, would share the runtime with Flatseal, but its sandbox is filesystems=[home] only — cannot reach the box's data outside a home dir, which is the streamed case that matters); org.kde.ark (equivalent sandbox and runtime to PeaZip, fewer formats); org.xarchiver.Xarchiver (NOT on Flathub, 404).

cryptomator.name: Cryptomator
cryptomator.description: Client-side encryption for cloud folders — creates an encrypted vault on this box that mounts as a normal folder, so files are encrypted before they ever leave.
cryptomator.author: Skymatic GmbH
cryptomator._note: CATALOGUE DEFECT FIXED: roadmap/APP-CATALOG.md lists `org.cryptomator.Crypt`, which returns 404 from the Flathub API — that id does not exist. Correct id is org.cryptomator.Cryptomator. Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (website). NOT extra-data. Sandbox: filesystems=[home, host-etc:ro] + KeePassXC browser-server sockets; devices=[all]; sockets=[x11] ONLY — no wayland socket, so under the cage/labwc v2 stack it needs XWayland.

impression.name: Impression
impression.description: Writes an ISO or disk image to a USB stick or SD card PLUGGED INTO THIS BOX. It cannot see removable media attached to the device you are viewing from.
impression.author: Khaleel Al-Adhami
impression._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github login provider). Sandbox: NO static filesystem grants; reaches drives via system-bus talk to org.freedesktop.UDisks2 and the portal. STREAMED-MODEL WARNING — the sharpest in this batch: the drive list is the BOX's drives. Combined with the streamed session running as root (stream/pool.go:416 has no uid drop, no netns, no cgroup), a mis-click writes an image over one of the box's own disks. The description above is the mitigation; a confirm-step in the shell would be better.

metadata-cleaner.name: Metadata Cleaner
metadata-cleaner.description: Strips EXIF, author, GPS and other hidden metadata from documents, images, audio and video stored on this box before you share them.
metadata-cleaner.author: Metadata Cleaner Developers
metadata-cleaner._note: CATALOGUE DEFECT FIXED: roadmap/APP-CATALOG.md lists `fr.romainvigier.MetadataCleaner`, which the Flathub API reports is_eol=true (the project moved namespace). Shipping an EOL id gets a user a package that stops receiving updates. Correct current id is io.gitlab.metadatacleaner.metadatacleaner (is_eol=false, publisher verified by website). Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Sandbox: NO static filesystem grants and NO network — file access is portal-mediated only. Best-isolated app in this batch.

frog.name: Frog
frog.description: Extracts text from any image or screenshot by OCR, including QR codes, and copies it to the clipboard. Runs against images on this box.
frog.author: Tender Owl
frog._note: Flathub AppStream+summary API 2026-08-15: id resolves 200, arches [aarch64,x86_64], not EOL. Publisher verified (github login provider). Sandbox: filesystems=[xdg-pictures] only; shared=[network,ipc] (used to download Tesseract language packs). STREAMED-MODEL: OCR of an on-box image is fine; 'grab from screen' captures the BOX's virtual display, which is what the user is looking at, so it behaves as expected.
